title: Typed stream framing guide and sample SDK implementations (TS / Python / Go)
creator: Ethan Liu
description: Deliver a concise engineering guide and working examples for a typed stream framing protocol across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs. Goal: provide deterministic, minimal-ambiguity framing (envelope + typed metadata + payload) that supports incremental streaming tokens, tool/function call events, and structured output patches so downstream SDKs and app developers can interoperate with Redwood runtime streams without ad-hoc parsing. Output must include: 1) protocol spec (text + examples), 2) canonical encoder/decoder code for TS/PY/GO, 3) sample integration app that demonstrates streaming tool invocation, structured JSON patches, and resumable reconnects. This ticket covers the spec + first-pass implementations and test suites (unit + e2e harness using local runtime simulator).
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc explaining frame types, required headers, and error semantics published to Confluence link
Working encoder/decoder in TypeScript that passes unit tests for framing, backpressure handling, and reconnect semantics
Python implementation with identical wire semantics and integration tests comparing byte-for-byte frames against the TypeScript implementation
Go implementation able to consume streams produced by TS/PY implementations in the e2e harness
Example app (TS frontend + PY backend) demonstrating tool/function call invocation mid-stream, structured output incremental JSON patches, and graceful fallback to non-streaming response
PR with implementation and tests merged, with at least one approving review from runtime and one from DX SDK owner

notes: Design decision: choose small binary-safe envelope with a length-prefixed header + JSON metadata block followed by payload to ensure both text and binary tool payloads can be transported without delimiter collisions.

Trade-off: single-buffer framing vs chunked framing. We chose chunked frames with monotonic sequence IDs to support resumption and replay; this adds slight protocol overhead but simplifies reconnects.
Compatibility: Provide a fallback 'legacy-line' adapter that can emit newline-delimited JSON for older clients during a transition period (configurable on the runtime).

Security: metadata headers include non-sensitive routing hints only (model, seq_id, event_type). Keying sensitive info into headers was rejected; recommend encrypting payloads at transport layer (TLS) and relying on per-tenant auth tokens.

Observed edge-case: streaming of nested structured outputs (e.g., large JSON arrays) requires an incremental JSON-patch event type rather than naive chunking to avoid producing invalid partial JSON for consumers that want typed objects.
comments: 2026-03-02 Ethan Liu: Initial spec draft uploaded to Confluence. Focused on three frame kinds: CONTROL, PAYLOAD, PATCH. CONTROL carries routing and session signals; PAYLOAD carries token/text/binary chunks; PATCH carries typed JSON patches for structured outputs.

2026-03-04 Priya Shah: Implemented TS encoder/decoder prototype. PT: push PR to repo for review. Noted that Node's stream backpressure semantics require a small write buffer to avoid head-of-line stalls when using continuous batching in the runtime.

2026-03-05 Miguel Alvarez: Python port in progress. Rewrote the decoder to be iterator-friendly (async generator) to fit common asyncio patterns. Found divergence in handling of zero-length PAYLOAD frames; standardized to treat as keepalive instead of error.
2026-03-07 Lena Kim: Added Go consumer and e2e harness. Found a bug where reconnect sequence IDs were off by one when resuming from last ACK; pushed hotfix to PR 2265.

2026-03-08 Rahul (runtime): Reviewed spec. Request: include explicit guidance for model-variant fallbacks in CONTROL frames so SDKs can decide whether to continue streaming or switch to short-polling. Marked as blocker for the release notes.

2026-03-09 Design (Ava Rodriguez): Reviewed sample UI flows for tool-call events. Requested that tool-call frames include a 'confirmation_required' flag for UIs that must request explicit user confirmation before invoking side effects.
2026-03-10 Priya Shah: Opened PR 2248 for TS. Current status: two reviewers requested changes (test coverage for reconnect scenarios + more exhaustive malformed-frame tests).
